AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: Lumbar synovial cysts are relatively infrequent. Historically, these benign lesions have been treated with open excision, sometimes associated with fusion. The aim of this study is to compare Minimally Invasive Surgery (MIS) with Open Surgery (OS) for the treatment of lumbar synovial cysts.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Retrospective review of patients who underwent minimally invasive or open excision of lumbar synovial cysts. Clinical outcomes, recurrence rate and surgical complications were compared in the 2 groups.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: 37 cases were identified, of which 24 were MIS and 13 were OS. MIS was significantly more effective in improving leg pain and radicular symptoms. There was no statistical difference between the two groups with regards to improvements of back pain and neurogenic claudication. Postoperative length of hospital stay and postoperative pain were significantly reduced in the MIS group (respectively 15h vs 24h and 0.9/10 vs 4.7/10 - p<0.5). There were no statistical differences in duration of surgery, intra- or post- operative complications, no recurrence of cyst in either of the two groups and no patients required fusion at a later stage.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: In this study, Minimally Invasive Surgery for the treatment of lumbar synovial cysts appears to be more effective than Open Surgery in relieving radicular symptoms. Furthermore, MIS is better tolerated by patients and is potentially cost saving for the Health Service, due to the reduction in hospital stay and the reduced requirement for painkillers.
